item_6_tighten_p_strong_b.reviewer_note: 2023 International PCOS Guideline: adult clinical hyperandrogenism criteria include hirsutism, acne, alopecia. Weight gain and acanthosis nigricans are metabolic features kept for doctor questions, not primary Rotterdam criteria.

item_7_reconsider_rf_dizzy.reviewer_note: Standalone dizziness downgraded to see_soon with suppress_pattern=false. Fainting/syncope or dizziness+bleeding/pain remains urgent/emergency with suppress_pattern=true.

item_8_teen_definition.reviewer_note: Adolescent cap is keyed on gynaecological age <= 3 years since menarche when available, falling back to chronological age <= 19 only when menarche age is unknown.

red_flag_rules.reason: Possible ectopic pregnancy: pregnancy possibility combined with sharp unilateral or severe pelvic pain requires immediate emergency evaluation.
Heavy bleeding during possible pregnancy requires immediate emergency evaluation.
Sudden severe ('thunderclap') headache is a neurological red flag requiring immediate emergency care.
Rapid onset voice deepening or virilisation requires urgent clinical workup to rule out androgen-secreting tumours or NCAH.
Severe pelvic pain with fever or fainting requires immediate evaluation to rule out ovarian torsion or acute pelvic infection.
Sudden severe pelvic pain requires prompt in-person medical evaluation.
Heavy menstrual bleeding accompanied by dizziness or fainting can indicate acute anaemia/hypovolaemia.
Fainting / loss of consciousness requires urgent medical assessment.
Heavy prolonged bleeding warrants prompt medical evaluation.
Dizziness combined with pelvic pain requires urgent evaluation.
Isolated dizziness warrants a routine medical check (e.g., haemoglobin/iron and blood pressure).

pattern_rules.description: Both irregular ovulation clues and clinical hyperandrogenism (hirsutism) are present.
Irregular cycles with multiple androgenic skin/scalp signals.
Irregular cycles combined with acne or metabolic/insulin-resistance clues (neck skin darkening or weight changes).
Single isolated hormonal or metabolic symptom noted.

confounder_rules.note: Within 3 years of menarche (or early adolescence), irregular cycles and acne are common during normal maturation.
Thyroid conditions can closely mimic PCOS cycle changes; TSH testing is essential.
Breastfeeding or milky nipple discharge (hyperprolactinaemia) suppresses ovulation and can mimic PCOS; ask your doctor about a serum prolactin test.
Cycles can take 3–6 months to regulate after stopping hormonal contraception.
